sources.title: Undercurrents: How Conflict, Climate Change and the Environment Intersect in Yemen
sources.organization: adelphi research and the European Institute of Peace, under the Weathering Risk Peace Pillar
sources.temporal_coverage: Primary fieldwork in 2023–2024 and reported conditions/cases through 2024.
sources.methodology: Mixed methods: 2,283 survey respondents, 69 focus-group participants and 58 interviews across nine governorates.
sources.limitations: Security constrained access; comprehensive climate data and projections were lacking. Cases are not nationally representative estimates.

sources.title: UNDP Yemen: Building Resilience: Supporting Farmers to Face the Impact of Climate Change in Yemen
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, published by United Nations in Yemen
sources.temporal_coverage: FSRRP implementation and farmer accounts reported in March 2024, with project photos dated 2023.
sources.methodology: UNDP project feature using named farmer and implementing-partner accounts and reported project outputs.
sources.limitations: Programme reporting and attributed testimony, not an independent impact evaluation; no comparison group is provided.

sources.title: From Seasonal to Sustainable: Year-Round Farming
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
sources.temporal_coverage: FAO-supported Shibam interventions and farmer accounts reported in February 2026.
sources.methodology: FAO feature story based on project implementation and local farmer accounts in Shibam.
sources.limitations: Project feature, not an independent evaluation; outcomes are reported by FAO and participants.

sources.title: Addressing Community Needs While Redressing the Impact of Climate Change in Yemen
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, Regional Bureau for Arab States
sources.temporal_coverage: SIERY project implementation and local authority actions reported in April 2025.
sources.methodology: UNDP project feature describing local-authority investments and reported programme outputs.
sources.limitations: Promotional implementation account; it provides no independent impact design and some metrics lack denominators or baselines.

sources.title: Cluster Evaluation of FAO Resilience Activities in Yemen 2018–2024
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), Office of Evaluation
sources.temporal_coverage: FAO resilience activity period 2018–2024; date of the evaluation webpage not stated.
sources.methodology: FAO publisher-page summary of a cluster evaluation covering water-focused natural-resource management, agriculture, livestock and governance under the HDP nexus.
sources.limitations: Only the official webpage summary was accessible; the linked report returned 403 and its local detail was not verified.

claims.locator: PDF printed p. 19, case study 2, ‘Precipitation Changes and Combat Create Tensions over Water Resources in Khanfar, Abyan.’
claims.paraphrase: In Khanfar, climate-change-related rainfall shifts reportedly reduced Wadi Bana flow and irrigation; conflict had damaged or destroyed 85% of irrigation infrastructure by late 2023. Some farmers diverted water from downstream users, who feared violence.
claims.limitations: Qualitative case drawing on interviews and cited secondary sources; the 85% infrastructure figure is dated late 2023.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The case links climate-related rainfall shifts to reduced water/irrigation, and describes conflict damage and farmer diversion as creating downstream tension and feared violence.

claims.locator: PDF printed p. 23, case study 5, ‘Women Lead Conflict Resolution in Al-Malakha, Sana'a.’
claims.paraphrase: In Al-Malakha, a dam serving about 350 farmers had been a violent conflict flashpoint. A women’s unit in the local WUA helped negotiate permitted shallow wells and a pipeline; the approach was replicated in 14 other villages with armed conflict.
claims.limitations: The case reports a 2018 mediation result; it does not establish that reduced rainfall caused the dispute.

claims.locator: UN in Yemen page, ‘Floods and rising temperatures’ and ‘Enhancing food security’ sections.
claims.paraphrase: In Al-Sukhnah and Al-Mansouriyah, Hodeidah, UNDP reports floods and heatwaves damaging farmland and crops; SFD reported 379 spillways across the districts, nearly 100 hectares benefited by reservoirs and 299 hectares protected by spillways.
claims.limitations: Area figures are project-officer-reported outputs; the page gives no independent measurement or counterfactual.

claims.locator: UN in Yemen page, ‘Empowering women farmers’ and ‘Combating drought and climate change’ sections.
claims.paraphrase: A named farmer in Sanif Al-Monasarah, Al-Mansouriyah, said spillways prevented soil erosion and helped restore irrigation; a project account says the work enabled her to return to crop production after land degradation had stopped cultivation.
institutions: Food Security Response and Resilience Project
claims.limitations: Individual participant account in a programme feature; no systematic gender-disaggregated outcome data are provided.

claims.paraphrase: In Wadi Bin Ali, Shibam, a farmer reported leaving fields uncultivated for months because seasonal spate irrigation, damaged canals and poor floodwater retention constrained production; beekeeping supplemented income.
claims.limitations: Single farmer's reported circumstances in an FAO programme feature; not a prevalence estimate.

claims.locator: FAO feature, ‘Response’ and ‘Aspirations and impact’ sections.
claims.paraphrase: FAO reports that Shibam interventions distributed over 70 greenhouses, targeted 102 agricultural facilities for rehabilitation and used two 45-day cash-for-work phases benefiting 1,900 people; the feature reports year-round production and fewer harvest failures.
claims.limitations: Reported project outputs and participant observations; the feature does not provide a counterfactual or evaluation design.

claims.locator: UNDP page, opening paragraphs on resource management, recovery and peacebuilding.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP states that Yemen's climate and water pressures, compounded by conflict, have harmed resource management and impeded recovery and peacebuilding.
claims.limitations: Broad programme narrative; it does not test a causal effect or identify a specific local pathway.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNDP says climate/resource pressures compounded by conflict impede recovery and peacebuilding.

claims.locator: UNDP page, ‘Disaster response and waste management’ and ‘Canal rehabilitation in Hadramaut’ sections.
claims.paraphrase: For flood-prone Mukalla and Seiyun, SIERY equipped local authorities to manage flood waste, improve drainage and rehabilitate rural roads; in Hadramaut, the project also rehabilitated irrigation canals for local agriculture.
claims.limitations: Implementation account; project-level efficiency and income percentages elsewhere on the page lack full baselines/denominators and are not repeated here.

claims.locator: FAO publisher summary, evaluation findings paragraph.
claims.paraphrase: FAO's evaluation summary says water-focused initiatives showed potential for area-based resilience and strengthened water-user associations, but short project periods, weak programme coherence and limited institutional ownership constrained sustainability; evidence of wider system change was limited.
claims.limitations: Only the FAO webpage summary was inspected; underlying evaluation report was inaccessible and summary has no local breakdown.

access_audit.notes: Full publisher-hosted report read directly; local cases distinguish source-reported pathways from interview-based fears and study limitations.
access_audit.reuse_terms: CC BY-ND 4.0 as stated in report imprint; claims are original factual paraphrases, with no figures or graphics reproduced.

access_audit.notes: Directly read the UN in Yemen publisher page; outputs and farmer statements remain programme-attributed.

access_audit.locator: Complete FAO feature page, especially ‘Seasonal agriculture,’ ‘Response’ and ‘Aspirations and impact.’
access_audit.notes: Publisher body read directly; distinguishes one farmer's experience from programme-level reported outputs.

access_audit.locator: Complete UNDP feature page, opening, disaster response and water-management sections.
access_audit.notes: Directly read the UNDP publisher page; programme reporting and broad climate-conflict statements are attributed to UNDP.

access_audit.notes: Official page was read; linked evaluation report returned HTTP 403, so only explicit publisher summary is used.
Repeated direct page requests timed out; indexed result was treated as a lead only and no findings were used.

access_audit.locator: UN Country Team 2024 Annual Report PDF.
access_audit.notes: Publisher PDF request exceeded the web reader's content-size limit; search-indexed text was not used for claims.
Read title and explicit prior-permission reproduction restriction; excluded all findings under source-use boundary.

search_audit.query: Yemen local climate conflict mechanisms, water access, rain variability, land disputes, and peacebuilding cases by district
search_audit.outcome: Read the full Weathering Risk assessment: it reports mediated pathways in Khanfar, water conflict/mediation in Al-Malakha and broader limitations; no climate-to-conflict inference was added beyond its explicit case wording.

search_audit.query: Yemen governorate and district climate vulnerability, flooding, drought, heat, agricultural livelihood local evidence 2024-2026
search_audit.outcome: Read local project accounts for Hodeidah flood/heat-affected farming and Hadramawt spate-irrigation constraints; local reports are programme accounts, not representative estimates.

search_audit.query: Yemen conflict damage displacement governance access constraints affecting water, flood response, climate adaptation
search_audit.outcome: The Khanfar case explicitly reports conflict damage to irrigation assets and constrained repair alongside rainfall/water pressures; SIERY and FAO sources show local-authority and programme capacities but do not isolate conflict's causal effect on their outcomes.

search_audit.query: Yemen local resilience capacity irrigation flood mitigation women farmer water user associations evaluation 2025 2026
search_audit.outcome: Read Hadramawt and Hodeidah intervention accounts, the Al-Malakha women's WUA mediation case, and FAO evaluation summary; sustainability and outcome evidence limitations are retained.

gaps: The FAO resilience evaluation report link returned HTTP 403; one claim is limited to the explicit publisher-page summary and has no local breakdown.
A 2024 UN Country Team report PDF was too large for the web reader, and a UNDP water-conflict story repeatedly timed out; their indexed text was not used.
A 2024 UNDP land-degradation report was excluded because its publisher notice requires prior permission to reproduce material.
The local climate-security fieldwork in the inspected full report is from 2023–2024; no newer directly read field study was found here. Project-feature claims are not independent impact estimates.
